assistant:
**Yes—in a same-time counterfactual, a corrective dispatch was feasible.** At the worst point, **19:30 on 5 January**, Bus_29 was at **0.944 p.u.**, below the **0.950 p.u.** limit; the assessment also found an overload on **Bus_0–Bus_1 [L0]**. The optimizer found a dispatch that brought Bus_29 to **0.950 p.u.** and met its limits. It increased each local generator’s active output by about **3.85–4.85 MW** and reduced external-grid import by **24.03 MW**. That shows a feasible corrective response at that moment—not that it was actually activated, or that the same action was available earlier.

**Warning:** the first sampled undervoltage was at **18:00**. The previous 15-minute sample, at **17:45**, was still in limits at **0.956 p.u.** So the data show only **15 minutes between the last in-limit reading and the first breach**; the voltage was already close to the lower limit. Bus_29 was below limit in **6 of 32** samples from 16:00–23:45, with the worst reading at 19:30.

These are historical simulation results, not an operations log: I can’t verify whether an alert was issued or a corrective action was actually taken. Measured active loads were assigned reactive demand using the default **0.95 lagging power factor**.

📋 Data source: measurements

assistant:
For the **18:30** reading, Bus_29 was at **0.945 p.u.**—below the **0.950 p.u.** limit—and **Bus_0–Bus_1 [L0]** was also overloaded. A corrective dispatch was feasible in the model at that timestamp: the optimizer brought Bus_29 to **0.950 p.u.** while meeting the specified limits. It increased local generation and reduced external-grid import by **23.49 MW**. This is a modeled counterfactual, not evidence that the dispatch was actually made; Bus_29 ends exactly at the limit, not with extra voltage margin.

The undervoltage episode had already started at **18:00**, so it was **30 minutes into the breach** by 18:30. The last in-limit sample was at **17:45**—just **15 minutes before onset**—at **0.956 p.u.** Thus the sampled data show little advance lead before the first breach.
